newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: No junior partners in APEC, leaders say.
newsitem.headline: No junior partners in APEC, leaders say.

text.p: APEC will not have second grade members, only full and equal partners, leaders in the 18-member Pacific Rim group said on Friday.

There will be "no junior partners but only equal partners", Philippines President Fidel Ramos said in an opening address to a meeting of foreign and trade ministers of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer told a news briefing that new membership in the organisation -- which aims to create a free trade and investment area covering half of humanity by 2020 -- was on hold until 1999.
"It appears that new membership is on hold until 1999 to give APEC a breathing space. In that period membership criteria will be refined and developed," he told a news briefing.
"We don't want to see a two-track or a three-track APEC. New members must fulfill all the achievements of APEC," he added.
APEC ministers, meeting ahead of the fourth annual APEC summit on Monday, were considering a membership package worked out earlier this week by senior officials.
A key element of the package is a "shadow individual action plan" under which applicants will have to prove their commitment to the APEC programme.
Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Thursday the 1997 summit in Vancouver would work out membership criteria and the 1998 summit in Kuala Lumpur would decide on new members.

APEC members are Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.

Several nations have expressed interest in joining, including India, Pakistan, Russia, Colombia, Ecuador and Mongolia. The Philippines and other Southeast Asian nations have expressed strong support for Vietnam to join as soon as possible.
